ShortDescription.Value: Control which buildings grow where, via custom zones and district themes.

Publish.LongDescription:
# Zone builder gives you the freedom to design custom zones down to the individual asset.
Tired of having to constantly switch between different residential zone types while filling out your suburbs? Want to build a city that adheres to one type of asset theme? Zone Builder is your tool to help speed up the zoning process while allowing you to build and manage a whole variety of zone themes.
## How it works
When using Zone Builder, you will navigate between three tabs, each covering one layer of zone hierarchy.
The zone hierarchy goes assets -> collections -> zones
### Assets tab
The assets tab is a grid or row list of all assets in game. This covers vanilla, custom, DLC, etc., across residential, commercial, office, and industrial. When not editing a collection, these are view-only. Assets can be searched by name, or narrowed down across a multitude of filters (pack, level, width, length)
### Collections tab
A collection is an "asset basket". Create a collection (example: US Rust Belt), and click add assets - you will be navigated to the assets tab. From there, you can begin choosing which assets you'd like to add. Add as many as you like! Once you're done, you can finalize your collection. Collections are editable at any time.
### Zones tab
These are your zones - each zone you create here will spawn a real zone in the game's zone tab. You will need to classify if this zone is NA or EU, and the zone's base type (Residential Low/Med/High/Mixed Use/Low Rent, Commercial Low/High, Office Low/High, Industrial). Once your zone is created, it is selectable and paintable in-game, just like any other zone. **But wait!** Zones need collections to spawn - make sure you edit your zone, assign it a collection, or multiple collections should you wish, and save. From there - paint away, and watch your chosen assets spawn!
Known quirks and limitations:
* Zones you create will show up in platter as soon as you create them. Zones you delete will remain in platter until you restart the game. * Lag on assigning collections to zones. With a large collection, you will notice a good lag when assign that collection to a zone. There will be UI showing load progress - however this lag is normal, as the game is cloning assets to be used in the new zone. * Find It: assets in collections will show as duplicates in Find It, however with a naming convention that distinguishes it from the original asset. There is no away around this currently.
### AI disclosure policy
I strongly believe in being 100% upfront about when and how AI is used, and where used, how exactly it was used. This mod's code was written through agents. Each scoped feature was validated through unit testing as well as UAT (human UAT) in-game. This UAT included confirming an existing feature works, it did not break other features, and compatibility with other zone-related mods did not change. Human involvement was present at each and every step of the way, and all architectural decisions and feature tradeoffs were made by humans, but the code itself is AI-written. Artwork (there's basically no artwork) was human-made. Github repo is linked to this mod and public, for those who wish to check it out.
Publish.ChangeLog:
New zone base types: Mixed Use and Low Rent are now their own choices alongside Residential Low/Medium/High, instead of buildings from those categories showing up unexpectedly inside a Medium or High density zone.
Zone creation now always uses a real vanilla NA/EU zone as its base - it will never pick up a zone added by another mod or asset pack by mistake.
Removing a building from a collection now warns you if that building is already grown somewhere in a zone using it, so you know before closing the game that it would turn into a white box next load. A new "Clean Up Orphaned Buildings" button (Settings > Zone Builder > Maintenance) can remove any building that's already become unrecoverable this way - the lot stays zoned and can regrow from the zone's current list.
Assets tab filters (zone, level, width, depth, pack) are now multi-select, so you can narrow by more than one value at once. Removed the unused "District Themes" checkbox from settings. Fixed collection edits from the Collections tab's own remove button triggering a full zone rebuild per click instead of once when you're done.
